subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: For the optional authenticated `POST /api/v1/admin/rpc` route in trusted-proxy deployments, is the existing explicit Origin policy the intended CSRF boundary, or must browser-originated mutations also present a per-request anti-CSRF token?
rationale: Source inspection disproves the reported ACP HTTP-file path, but deciding whether defense-in-depth tokens are required for the separate optional admin HTTP surface is a security policy choice with compatibility consequences for existing host automation.

options.title: Keep Origin Boundary
options.body: Confirm that Gateway HTTP authentication, method scopes, and explicit allowed-origin validation are the supported CSRF boundary, then request a concrete bypass before further code changes.

options.title: Require CSRF Tokens
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped token mechanism for browser-originated admin HTTP mutations while preserving non-browser authenticated automation clients.

options.title: Disallow Browser Admin RPC
options.body: Reject browser-originated requests on the optional admin HTTP route entirely and document it as host-automation-only.

recommendation.title: Keep Origin Boundary
recommendation.body: Confirm that Gateway HTTP authentication, method scopes, and explicit allowed-origin validation are the supported CSRF boundary, then request a concrete bypass before further code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the current shared trusted-proxy HTTP origin-policy boundary most directly involved in this decision.
